subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If 1, ω, ω² are the cube roots of unity, show that (a + b)(aω + bω²)(aω² + bω) = a³ + b³.

Re-derived: (aω + bω²)(aω² + bω) = a² − ab + b², times (a + b) is a³ + b³; the book's answer is correct.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — what the two ω brackets multiply to, and which factorisation finishes it.
insider_note: Multiply the two ω brackets first — putting (a + b) in first gives a cubic in ω that does not simplify. The second mark is recognising a² − ab + b² as the factor that makes (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) = a³ + b³.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply the two ω brackets
steps.margin_note: First mark. (aω + bω²)(aω² + bω) = a²ω³ + abω² + abω⁴ + b²ω³. With ω³ = 1 and ω⁴ = ω this is a² + ab(ω + ω²) + b², and ω + ω² = −1 gives a² − ab + b².
lines: = a² + ab(ω² + ω) + b²  (ω³ = 1, ω⁴ = ω)

steps.why: Every ω question is the same two facts: ω³ = 1 (so high powers of ω reduce) and 1 + ω + ω² = 0 (so any two of 1, ω, ω² can be replaced by minus the third). The reduction is the mark; the arithmetic after it is short.
common_mistakes: Writing ω⁴ = ω² and getting 2abω² instead of ab(ω + ω²).
Writing ω + ω² = 1 and getting a² + ab + b².
Multiplying (a + b) in first and getting a cubic in ω.

steps.label: Multiply by (a + b)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. a² − ab + b² is the second factor of a³ + b³, so (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) = a³ + b³. No ω is left in the answer.

recall.must_convey: That the reduced expression is evaluated to a³ + b³.
